newsitem.title: UK: Greenpeace activists hold out on BP oil platform.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace activists hold out on BP oil platform.

text.p: Greenpeace activists chained to a mobile oil platform in the Atlantic were determined to stay on after boarding the British Petroleum rig two days ago, the environmental group said Monday.
Two activists of the original seven who climbed the Stena Dee platform on Saturday to protest development of the Foinaven oilfield northwest of Scotland were still on the rig.
Greenpeace wants the Stena Dee to return to Norway and called on BP to abandon the Foinaven project, the first to be developed in deep waters west of the Shetland Islands.

A Greenpeace spokeswoman said the oil rig was 50 miles northwest of the Orkney islands and 22 miles south of the Foinaven field, the first of BP's Atlantic Frontier drilling operations scheduled to produce oil.
"Safety-wise they're fine," a Greenpeace spokeswoman said, adding that no efforts were being made to get the campaigners off the platform.
The two German activists -- one male, one female -- have been chained on one of the Stena Dee's legs since midday on Sunday, BP said.
A BP spokesman said the company's priority at the moment was the safety of all on board the rig, which was heading from Norway to work on Foinaven.
"Protecting the climate is not an optional extra, it is an absolute necessity. We're here for the duration," campaigner Liz Pratt on board of a Greenpeace vessel said in a statement.
The BP spokesman said Greenpeace's action would not delay the oil company's operations at the much-delayed Foinaven, which is now expected to produce oil by the end of the year.
The project has suffered a series of technological mishaps. It was originally due onstream the middle of 1996.
